steps.text: In a large pot with boiling salted water cook spaghetti pasta until al dente. Drain.
Meanwhile, in a large skillet over low heat saute garlic, parsley, and red pepper flakes with olive oil . Cook until garlic turns golden in color, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Toss pasta with garlic mixture and butter or margarine. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Pasta e Olio
raw_recipe.description: In just a matter of minutes you can whip up this simply splendid dish of pasta and olive oil, heady with garlic and seasoned with parsley and red pepper flakes. Finish with a generous coating of melted butter and serve warm.
raw_recipe.name: Pasta e Olio

review.reviewBody: With the exception of the cayenne pepper, this is the traditional pasta with garlic and olive oil I grew up with in my Italian family. If anything, we add a bit of crushed red pepper flakes to taste, but it is just as traditional and tasty without. This is the Italian version of buttered noodles--and it's darn good. Also delicious with a sprinkle of grated fresh Parmesan or Romano cheese.

This reminds me of a recipe I make that I saw on the Rachel Ray show. It's Quick, Easy, and Pasta....who can ask for more! While I'm boiling my water for my lb. of pasta (I use wheat pasta) I use my food processor to combine 2 bunches of flat leaf parsley, 2 cloves of garlic, enough olive oil to make a paste and salt and pepper to taste. Next I saute a couple of handful of pine nuts in olive oil....watch carefully so they do not burn. When they begin to brown add 1/2 cup of breadcrumbs to brown. Then add your parsley mixture and cook a few more minutes. Mix everything above with your cooked pasta, squeeze in the juice of one lemon and add fresh shredded parm cheese and garnish with a couple of chopped plum tomatoes.

This was excellent and easy! I only sauteed the garlic for a few min (personal preference). To me, it would be a bit bland without adding the crushed red pepper flakes. They really kick it up a notch! I also added a little of the water from the pasta, used dried parsley and topped with salt, pepper and Romano cheese. I had this with Chicken Milanese from this site. It could be a side dish or a main dish. Thanks for this great recipe!

As it was written not a fan, too oily and greasy and the garlic just wasn't right. I saw the potential in it though so the second time around I essentially simplified it, I added just a splash of olive oil to the noodles after cooking, melted the butter in a pan with the red pepper, garlic powder and a little dried parsley. Shut off the burner, tossed the noodles in the pan and mixed in a good amount of fresh parsley, salt and pepper, and a touch of lemon juice to brighten it up a bit. It was perfect, served with lemony steamed fish recipe.

**EXCELLENT** Made it to accompany a very tasty but plain looking chicken breast for a group of 30 people & EVERYONE raved! Simple but so flavorful, just the right amount of kick from the red pepper flakes & I am not a fan of hot/spicy dishes & this is far from that so I would not alter this recipe at all for the 1st time you try it. I grated fresh Parmesan over the entire thing right off the heat then tong tossed it all together with just a bit of the pasta water...the pasta water & Parmesan give this dish the salt needed to take it from great tasting to outstanding! I will use this recipe over & over again, thank you so much for sharing!

I made two changes: when mixing the oil/butter sauce to the pasta, I added about 1/3 cup pasta water and a generous handful of fresh grated Parmesan. These small revisions made for a delicious side dish. I generously salted the pasta water (1 1/2 - 2 tablespoons) prior to cooking the pasta. This dish is a keeper.

Very good and easy to make on a busy work night. Because I have a picky three-year-old, I ommitted the red pepper, but added fresh mushrooms and zucchini, as well as two sliced, leftover grilled chicken breasts from last night's dinner. I sauteed all of the vegetables and chicken slices in the oil, parsley, and garlic, and blended it with the butter and pasta. Served with grated parmesan cheese, it was great!

I vary this recipe with 1/2 c olive oil heated in a saucepan, add 1 cup diced pepperoni, 2 tablespoons garlic and about 1/4 teaspoon of red pepper flakes. Add a handful of chopped parsley. Make sure when you add the garlic you only let it get blond in color. The worst thing for this dish is burning the garlic. If this seems dry add about 1/2 to 1 cup of pasta water and it will be perfect. Just remember when draining the pasta to save some of the pasta water. This is a nice alternative to rice or potato for a side dish.

couldn't have been quicker or easier. I had everything on hand and even added cooked shrimp (bought frozen deveined, cooked, tails removed and thawed in water for a few minutes- I added it the last couple of minutes just to warm it through). I will double the garlic. 10 minutes is too long- it will burn. 5 minutes probably. I think it's too much pasta for the amount of sauce though.

This is such a delicious, classic pasta dish! We have this often, and I always add more garlic. Most of the time I omit the pepper flakes, just serve with the dish at the table. For a different variation, saute some chopped broccoli with the oil mixture, we love it this way. Freshly chopped basil is also very good, use that instead of the parsley. Be sure to top with plenty of freshly grated parmesan cheese when served. :)

I was pleasantly surprised to find that heating the olive oil with the garlic & pepper gave the pasta sort of a nutty, mellow flavor. I wanted to add a veggie to this dish, so wilted some fresh spinach with the pasta water and then added all into the skillet to saute together for a minute or so in the butter.
This is a classic pasta dish, no frills. I would make it again but with a little bit more olive oil.
It end up kind of dry, and I think I used the wrong oil. My boyfriend love it.

So so so so good! I didn’t add cayenne pepper because I wanted my toddler to try it but regardless it was delicious. I cooked for my mom, sis, and hubby and they all said it was perfect. I paired it with a chicken piccata recipe from Allrecipes as well.

I followed it almost exactly, but since I didn’t have fresh parsley, I added dry parsley instead, about half of the recipe amount, added some dry basil, very little. My kids loved it! And they are very picky eaters!

I made this recipe as written, other than adding a couple of extra cloves of chopped garlic, (just personal preference- I'm a garlic lover). It was tasty and easy to make. I'll definitely make this again!
